name: Second Chance
blurb: She wakes up five years in the past, one day before the deal that ruined her family
title: Second Chance: Rebirth Short Drama Script (Episode 1)
description: A free 3-minute vertical rebirth short drama script for 4 actors. She wakes five years earlier, the day before a deal ruins her family. Free to film.
h1: Second Chance: a 3-Minute Rebirth Short Drama Script, Episode 1
logline: Lena lost her family's home and factory to one bad contract and a fiancé who vanished with the money. Then she wakes up five years earlier, the morning before her father signs, and she remembers every hidden clause.
setting: A bedroom, a family kitchen and a small office. Props: two phones, a thick printed contract, coffee mugs, orange juice, a pen.

roles.name: Lena
roles.note: Late 20s, woke up five years in the past; grief turned into focus.

roles.name: Daniel
roles.note: 50s, her father, a proud factory owner who trusts too easily. Can be a mother with small edits.

roles.name: Ethan
roles.note: 30s, Lena's fiancé; charming, helpful, secretly working with Cross.

roles.name: Vincent
roles.note: 50s, the investor, Vincent Cross; smooth, patient, knows more than anyone thinks. Any gender.

script.action: LENA, late twenties, jolts awake, gasping. She grabs her phone. The lock screen shows the date. She stares at it.

script.say: No. No, no. This is the day before.

script.action: She touches her face, her hair, the old phone case she threw away years ago. Then she runs.
Her father, DANIEL, fifties, in a pressed shirt, reads a thick contract over coffee. Lena's fiancé ETHAN, thirties, pours orange juice like he lives there.

script.say: Morning, sweetheart. Big day tomorrow. Mr. Cross signs at ten and the factory is saved.
Dad. Don't sign it.
Bad dream?
Five years of one.

script.action: She takes the contract and flips straight to the back, as if she knows the page.

script.say: Clause fourteen. If the warehouse is damaged, all its debts move to you personally. The house, the factory, everything.
The warehouse is fine. It's brand new.
It floods in March. The whole ground floor. And the insurance is in Mr. Cross's brother's name, not yours.
Lena, how could you possibly know that?

script.action: Lena looks at him. Really looks. She remembers something.

script.say: Because you told me. Five years from now. Right before you left with the money.
Lena!
Dad, his passcode is the date he met Mr. Cross. Not my birthday. Ask him to unlock his phone.

script.action: Ethan's hand tightens on his phone. He doesn't move.

script.say: Ethan. Unlock it.
This is insane. I'm not going to be interrogated over breakfast.

script.action: He walks out. The front door slams. Daniel sits very still.

script.say: He didn't even try to unlock it.

script.action: VINCENT CROSS, fifties, smooth and smiling, slides a pen across the desk. Daniel does not pick it up. Lena stands beside him.

script.say: Daniel. Everything is ready. Your factory, saved by lunch.
We'd like to change clause fourteen. And put the insurance in my father's name.
Your daughter has been reading the small print.
And the warehouse survey. The one you paid to keep in a drawer.
No deal today, Vincent. Maybe no deal at all.

script.action: Daniel stands. Lena follows him to the door. Vincent's voice stops her.

script.say: Lena. Stay a moment.

script.action: Daniel steps outside. Vincent leans back in his chair, studying her.

script.say: Clause fourteen. The flood. The brother. And the passcode.
I don't know what you mean.
You do. Because last time, you said exactly the same thing, word for word.
Welcome back, Lena. This time, I remember too.

body: Shoot vertical 9:16. Light the bedroom cool and dim for the waking shot, then make the kitchen bright and warm so the past feels like a safe place about to break. The office can be any desk against a plain wall with a chair that leans back. Keep the phone on a tripod for the office scene so Vincent's final speech has a slow, still, controlled feel, and go handheld in the kitchen for urgency. Record dialogue close to the actors; three takes of Vincent's last two lines, each a little quieter, will give you the best ending.

ul: Lena has already lived the worst five years. Play her as tired and certain, not shocked; she only panics in the first ten seconds.
Ethan must be likeable at first. His mistake is one line said a beat too fast; make that the only crack until he refuses to unlock the phone.
Daniel's heartbreak is quiet. He didn't even try to unlock it should be almost under his breath.
Vincent never raises his voice. The menace comes from how relaxed he is, as if the whole scene bores him.
Pause before Welcome back. Let Lena's face show the floor dropping away, then deliver the final line gently.
Avoid overacting the waking shot. One sharp breath and a long stare at the phone tells the audience everything.
Change the deal: instead of a factory contract, it is the sale of the family's restaurant, signed over a meal in the restaurant itself.
Make the reborn character a son and the parent a mother, or make Ethan a trusted business partner instead of a fiancé.
Give part two a different hook: the person who also remembers is not Vincent but Daniel, who has been pretending all along.

faq.q: Can I use this rebirth script for a paid short drama app or channel?
faq.a: Yes. It is free under CC BY 4.0, including commercial use. Credit "Script: cv.cm" in the episode description or the credits.

faq.q: How do I show the time jump on a low budget?
faq.a: Use the phone date, the caption and one prop from the past, like an old phone case or a hairstyle Lena no longer has. A quick blur or a flash cut on waking is enough; no special effects are needed.

faq.q: Why does Vincent remember, and where does episode 2 go?
faq.a: That is the hook. Episode 1 only shows that Lena is not the only one who came back. You can decide whether Vincent caused the jump, lived the same loop, or is bluffing because Ethan told him everything.
